threads.body: Calling this method alone only enables Reactor's restoration of values exposed through Micrometer Context Propagation; it does not register an accessor for OpenTelemetry `Context`. This module does not register a `ThreadLocalAccessor`, so users following this condition can still lose the active OTel context. Require automatic propagation to be configured specifically for OpenTelemetry context.
threads.hunk:
@@ -83,6 +83,23 @@ public class WebClientConfig {
 }
 ```
 
+### Reactor context propagation hook
+
+Spring WebFlux runs on Project Reactor, which can switch threads across a reactive pipeline. 
+OTel context is stored in a `ThreadLocal` and will not survive these switches without the Reactor context propagation hook.
+
+**When you need the hook:**
+Use `createWebFilterAndRegisterReactorHook()` and `addFilterAndRegisterReactorHook()` which register the hook for you.
+This is the case when using library instrumentation without the Java agent and without Reactor's own automatic context propagation.
+
+**When you do NOT need the hook:**
+- You are using OpenTelemetry Java agent - it registers the hook automatically.
+- Your application already calls `Hooks.enableAutomaticContextPropagation()`. 
+  Adding the OTel hook on top is unnecessary and can cause increased memory allocation.
+  Use `createWebFilter()` and `addFilter()` instead.
